title: Peach and Raspberry Smoothie
description: Blend up a refreshing kidney-friendly peach and raspberry smoothie! This delicious, easy to make recipe is perfect for a healthy, fruity treat.
steps: Put the peaches and raspberries into a blender.
Pour the Renastep into the blender with the peaches and raspberries and blend until smooth.
Serve and enjoy!

title: Pasta Salad
description: This quick and simple pasta salad can be whipped up in 15 minutes using just five ingredients. Ideal after a long day. Learn how to make it.
steps: Boil the pasta until fully cooked, rinse with cold water and set aside to cool.
In a large bowl mix together pasta, cucumber and feta.
Whisk together olive oil and lemon juice until emulsified.
Pour over the pasta mix and mix until thoroughly coated.
Serve and enjoy!
hints: Renastep note

title: Low Tomato Bolognese Sauce with Meatballs
description: A low tomato version of Meatballs with Bolognese sauce which creates a flavoursome, savory staple for those on a renal diet. Try cooking it tonight.
ingredients: 1 reduced salt chicken or beef stock cube with 200ml water
steps: Preheat the oven to 180ºC / 160ºC Fan / 350ºF / Gas mark 4.
Divide the 400g of minced beef into 16 evenly sized meatballs and roll them into shape. Then put the meatballs onto a baking tray.
Cook the meatballs in the oven for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the onions, carrots and celery for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and fry for a further minute.
Add the stock, passata, basil and nutmeg and season to taste with salt and pepper.
Simmer on a low heat for about an hour. Put the lid of the pan slightly ajar to let out the steam.

Add the sauce to the cooked meatballs. Serve with pasta and garlic bread. This recipe is taken from the Kidney Friendly Cookbook produced by Dietitians and Dietetic Support Workers at a Paediatric Renal Unit in the UK. Please check with your Dietitian or Doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Filo Fish Pie
description: This simple fish pie recipe contains only five ingredients and takes just 25 minutes to prepare. Ideal as a main meal for four people.
ingredients: 300g frozen fish pie mix (Salmon and prawn mix - defrosted)
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C/320°F/Gas mark 3
In a large pan, place the frozen fish mixture and cover with the rice milk, allow to simmer until the fish is just cooked.
Remove the fish and place into a bowl, pour the milk into a jug and set aside.
Place ½ the melted butter into a pan and add the flour, allow to cook until combined.
Gradually add the milk to the pan, ensuring to whisk away any lumps, continue adding until the mixture is a thick sauce and can coat the back of a spoon.
Add the fish mixture back to the sauce and pour into a circular oven dish.
Scrunch the filo pastry into balls and place on top of the fish mixture, ensuring to coat the filo with the remaining butter.
Bake for 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Remove from the oven, serve and enjoy!
hints: Renastep note
Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Tofu tacos
description: Try these zesty tofu tacos with seasoned crumbles, fresh toppings, and creamy sauce - flavourful, protein-packed, and perfect for taco night.
steps: Heat the oil in a pan and add red peppers and onions, cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add in the paprika, cumin, coriander and chilli flakes, cook until peppers and onions are soft. Then remove from heat and place into a bowl.
Heat the oil in the same pan, fry the tofu until golden brown on both sides.
Once golden, remove from pan and set aside.
In another bowl place the mashed peas, olive oil, garlic, coriander and lime juice and mix together well.
Place wraps onto a plate and place the peppers, onions, tofu, and pea guacamole onto the wraps.
Fold up the bottom of the wraps and then fold the sides over.
Serve and enjoy!

title: Macaroni Cheese
description: A twist on the classic Macaroni Cheese makes this suitable for those on a renal diet. Enjoy this comforting classic while catering for kidney disease.
ingredients: 40g full fat garlic and herb soft cream cheese
steps: Preheat oven to 190°C/375°F/Gas Mark 4
Place the macaroni into a saucepan of boiling water. Boil for 9-10 minutes whilst stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, place the vegetable margarine into a saucepan and heat on low until melted.
Add the flour to the pan and stir until the mixture forms a smooth paste. Cook on a low heat for approximately 2 minutes.
Pour half of the Renastep into the pan and allow to boil without stirring.
Stir until the mixture blends smoothly and then beat with a whisk. Add the remaining Renastep to the mixture and stir in until it is all combined.
Take off the heat and stir in the soft cream cheese, emmental cheese, wholegrain mustard and pepper.
When the pasta is cooked, drain and add the sauce. Stir well until it is all combined together.
Place the mixture into an oven proof dish, sprinkle with nutmeg and bake in the oven for 25 minutes.
hints: Renastep note
Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision.

description: Enjoy a renal-friendly pineapple smoothie. This tropical refreshing drink is suitable for the dietary management of kidney disease. Try it today!
steps: Place all the ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth.

title: Çiğ Köfte
description: This kidney-friendly Çiğ Köfte recipe made with rice, breadcrumbs, herbs, and spices makes a flavourful, plant-based dish and cooks in 15 minutes.
steps: Boil the rice until it becomes mushy, drain the water and blend until smooth. Place into a bowl.
Add the breadcrumbs to the bowl of rice and stir together until well combined.
Add grated onion, harissa, garlic, olive oil, tomato puree, chipotle paste, chili flakes, and black pepper, cumin to the mixture and knead together.
Sprinkle with spring onions, parsley and lemon juice.
Roll the mixture into 20 small balls and place on a plate. Serve and enjoy!
hints: Renastep note
Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Borscht
description: Learn how to cook this hearty, vibrant borscht soup made with beets, cabbage, and fresh herbs - rich, tangy, and comforting in every spoonful.
steps: Heat the butter in a pan and add the onions, carrot and celery and allow to soften slightly.
Add in beetroot and garlic and combine with the other vegetables.
Crumble the stock cubes into the vegetable mixture and then add the coriander seeds, black pepper, bay leaf and butterbeans.
Cover with water and allow to simmer for 20 minutes.
Once cooked blend until smooth.
Stir in the lemon juice and serve with sour cream and dill.

title: Beef Stroganoff
description: Enjoy this quick, kidney-friendly Beef Stroganoff recipe which can be made in just 25 minutes, ideal with pasta for a filling main meal.
ingredients: 1 low salt beef stock cube e.g. Kallo
steps: Heat oil in a pan, add sliced onion, leeks, garlic, and cook until soft
Add in the beef chunks, cannellini beans, black pepper and smoked paprika. Cook for 2 minutes and then add in the flour.
In a jug add a beef stock cube, dijon mustard, Renastep and boiling water and stir until fully combined.
Pour over the wet mixture and mix well ensuring that all the beef juices and flour are combined.
Allow to simmer for 10 minutes or until thickened.
Serve over pasta and enjoy!

title: Borek
description: Cook this flaky, golden Turkish Börek filled with savory cheese or meat, perfect for breakfast, snacks, or gatherings - easy, crispy, and delicious!
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Place kale into boiling water for 1 minute. Then remove from bowl and thoroughly dry.
Finely chop kale and combine with feta and cottage cheese in a bowl and set aside.
Place two sheets of filo pastry onto your baking sheet, brush both with butter then place another 2 sheets on top.
Place the cheese and kale mix onto the pastry and spread out evenly across the baking tray.
Layer the remaining sheets of filo on top ensuring to butter between layers.
Brush the top layer with egg and bake for 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Remove from oven slice into portions and enjoy!

title: Apple purée
description: A super quick and easy first food recipe designed to get your child used to solids. Make in just twenty minutes. Note you'll need a blender.
ingredients: 2 sweet apples e.g. Royal Gala, Pink Lady, Golden Delicious
steps: Peel apples.
Chop the apples in to small pieces.
Place the apple in a saucepan.
Add a dash of water and boil until soft, approximately 10 -12 minutes.
Once cooled, whizz the apples in a blender until smooth.
hints: Add a pinch of cinnamon for extra flavour

title: Fish Fingers
description: Crispy and flavorful fish fingers recipe. Learn how to make delicious homemade fish fingers that the whole family will love. Suitable for a renal diet.
ingredients: 50g breadcrumbs (blitz 1-2 slices of bread in a food processor or grater)
steps: Cut the fish fillets into 8 fingers.
Set out 3 bowls; one with the beaten egg in, 1 with the flour in and one with the cornflakes and breadcrumbs in.
One at a time, coat the raw fish in flour, then dip into the beaten egg mixture before finally coating in the cornflakes or breadcrumbs, making sure you coat all the fish evenly.

Carefully fill a frying pan with rapeseed, vegetable or sunflower oil about 1 cm deep to shallow fry. Heat the oil, to test the temperature, drop a cornflake in, it should sizzle slowly and gently brown over 20-30 seconds. If the bread coating browns too quickly and burns, the oil it too hot.
Fry the fish for about 3 minutes each side. Be careful not to splash the hot oil.
hints: Serve with polenta chips and peas.
Be aware of the potassium content in any accompanying vegetables

title: Apple Porridge With Blueberry Compote
description: Start your day with a delicious Apple Porridge, a nutritious and hearty breakfast option, suitable for a renal diet and managing kidney disease.
steps: Mix the oats, grated apple, cinnamon and Renastep in a small saucepan.
Bring gently to the boil, stirring occasionally, then reduce heat and cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Meanwhile, tip the blueberries into a pan with 1 tsp of water and honey and gently poach until the blueberries have thawed and are tender, but still holding their shape.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the blueberries.
hints: Renastep note
Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision.

title: Easter Chick Cupcakes
description: Celebrate Easter with these adorable Easter Chick Cupcakes. These delightful treats will bring joy to your festivities and are suitable for a renal diet.
steps: To make the cupcakes
Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C Fan/Gas Mark 4.
To make the cupcakes
In a bowl, combine the flour and bicarbonate of soda.
To make the cupcakes
In a separate bowl, beat the egg, gradually add the sugar, vanilla extract and oil, and stir until combined.
To make the cupcakes
Add the flour mixture and half a bottle of Renastep (approx. 60ml) and whisk.
To make the cupcakes
Add the remaining half a bottle of Renastep to the mixture and whisk.
To make the cupcakes
Place the 4 x 8 cm diameter cupcake cases into a muffin tray and evenly pour the cake mixture into the cases.
To make the cupcakes
Bake in the oven for 15-20 minutes, until golden brown.
To make the cupcakes
Carefully transfer the cupcakes onto a wire rack to cool
For the frosting
Cream together the butter and icing sugar in a bowl.
For the frosting
Add half a bottle of Renastep (approx. 60ml) and the vanilla extract to the butter icing mixture and mix well.
For the frosting
Add the food colouring to get your desired colour.
To decorate
Spread the icing onto the surface of the four cupcakes evenly, using the back of a spoon.
To decorate
Dip the surface of the cupcakes into the coconut.
To decorate
Add the ‘eyes’ to each cupcake using 2 chocolate chips.
To decorate
Add a ‘beak’ to each cupcake using a small slice of cherry, cut into the shape of a triangle. Your Easter chicks are now ready.
hints: Renastep note
Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision.
Renastep note

title: Pomegranate Smoothie
description: This quick and easy pomegranate smoothie recipe is made with Renastep and takes just 10 minutes to make. It's suitable for those with kidney disease.
steps: Pour Renastep into a blender. Add the other ingredients and blend.
Pour into a glass. Serve cold.
hints: Swap frozen raspberries for blueberries if permitted. Serve over re-usable plastic ice cubes for a refreshing drink with less fluid.

title: Baklava
description: Learn how to make this delicious homemade baklava with pecans, hazelnuts, and a citrusy syrup. Crispy, nutty, and sweet - ready in just over an hour!
steps: Preheat the oven to 200˚C /180˚C fan / Gas Mark 6.
In a bowl, combine chopped pecans, pumpkin seeds, hazelnuts, cinnamon and cardamom with the honey.
Place a sheet of filo pastry into a 25x15cm baking tray and brush with butter. Continue this process until half the pack of pastry has been used.
Spread the nut mixture evenly over the pastry.
Place the other half of filo sheets on top of the nut mixture, continuing the buttering and layering process until the whole pack is used. Any remaining butter should be poured over the top.
Cut 12 portions into the baklava and bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Meanwhile, place the sugar and water into a pan with orange zest. Bring the syrup to a boil and then allow to simmer until it resembles runny honey.
Remove the baklava from the oven and pour all of the syrup over evenly.
Allow to cool fully before serving.

title: Vegetable Sambusa
description: Make this crispy kidney-friendly vegetable sambusa filled with spiced carrots, cauliflower, peas, and peppers to have as a savoury snack. Cooks in 20 minutes
steps: Heat oil in a pan and fry the onions, garlic and ginger until soft.
Once softened add in the cumin, garam masala and coriander, mix together for 2 minutes.
Then add in the carrots, cauliflower, peppers, and peas, stir together, and cook until soft. Set aside.
In a small bowl mix together the flour and water until a paste forms.
Place a small spoonful of the vegetable mixture onto 1 spring roll wrapper, Fold over the mixture and continue to fold in opposite directions until a triangle has formed.
Spread a small amount of the flour mixture at the opening of the triangle and press together to seal.
Heat enough oil in a pan to shallow fry (usually ¼ inch up the side of the pan). Test the temperature with a small amount of pastry, if it turns golden brown and bubbles, the oil is ready to fry.
Place the sambusa into the pan and cook on both sides until golden brown, remove from the pan and place onto kitchen paper.
Once slightly cooled serve and enjoy!

title: Rice Bukhari
steps: Preheat an oven to 180°C/356°F/Gas mark 4.
Onto a baking tray add the carrots and red pepper, drizzle with a little oil, and roast for 20-30 minutes or until soft.
Heat 1/2 the oil in a pan and add cloves and cardamom pods, allow to toast slightly.
Add onions, garlic, and allow to soften slightly.
Once softened, add in the chicken pieces and allow to brown slightly on all sides.
Once browned, add in the cinnamon, allspice, white pepper, dried lime powder, nutmeg, coriander, and cumin. Stir until the chicken is fully coated with the spices.
Remove the red pepper and carrots from the oven and add to a blender with enough stock to cover the vegetables and form a thin puree.
Blend until smooth and then add into the pan with the rest of the vegetable stock, stir well, and bring to boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and allow to simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add in the rice and cook for 10 minutes or until the liquid is fully absorbed.
Once cooked, place the rice on a plate and add the chicken on top and set aside.
Add the butter to a pan and melt, add in the macadamia nuts and pumpkin seeds and cook until slightly brown.
Pour the butter and nuts over the rice, serve and enjoy.

title: Chicken Nuggets
description: Make this homemade version of chicken nuggets, created with renal patients in mind. They are super quick to make in just 15 minutes. Try it today!
ingredients: 2 large chicken breasts, chopped into bite-size pieces
80g breadcrumbs (buy ready-made or grate some bread)
steps: Put the breadcrumbs in a bowl.
Put the yoghurt in a separate bowl.
Dip the raw chicken pieces into the yoghurt then coat in the breadcrumbs.
Shallow fry in oil (try rapeseed/sunflower oil) for about 5 minutes each side, but keep an eye on them to make sure they don’t start to burn!
hints: Add 2 tsp of sage for added flavour.
Serve these with polenta chips or chopped up into hot pasta with a knob of garlic butter.

title: Egg Muffins
description: Try these kidney-friendly Egg Muffins recipe from My Renal Nutrition, designed for individuals with renal disease, offering a nutritious and delicious meal option.
steps: Heat 1 tsp oil in a pan and fry broccoli and peppers with paprika and black pepper until soft.
Whisk eggs and Renastep in a bowl until fully combined.
Pour egg mixture evenly between each muffin cup.
Evenly distribute the cooked vegetables and crumbled feta between each muffin.
Bake for 15 minutes or until cooked through and serve.

title: Pea courgette purée
description: This recipes makes one portion of weaning suitable food which takes just 20 minutes to make and can have a thin consistency if required.
ingredients: 100ml of breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialized low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian)
steps: Cut the courgettes into small chunks.
Boil the courgette for 5 minutes.
Add frozen peas and boil for a further 3-4 minutes.
Drain vegetables and cool.
Add 100ml breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian).
Use a blender to whizz up to a purée consistency.
Add more breast milk, standard infant formula or the specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed if a thinner consistency is required.
Add into ice cube trays and freeze or use straight away.

title: Winter Warmer
description: Stay cosy with this comforting Winter Warmer Smoothie recipe which is suitable for a renal diet. Embrace the season with a quick to make warm drink.
steps: Place a pan over a medium heat and add all the ingredients.
Stir continuously to warm gently, do not boil.
Remove from the heat and whisk with a hand or electric whisk to make a frothy drink.
Serve warm.
hints: Serve with suitable biscuits such as gingerbread.

title: Blueberry Smoothie
description: Enjoy a refreshing, kidney-friendly blueberry smoothie! This easy recipe is low in potassium and packed with flavor—perfect for a healthy, delicious treat.
steps: Add the blueberries into a blender
Pour the Renastep into the blender with the blueberries and blend until smooth.
Serve and enjoy!

title: Easy Chicken Pizza
description: Discover an easy, nutritious chicken pizza recipe suitable for those on a renal diet. Try this delicious meal option which you can make in 15 minutes.
ingredients: 4 chunks of either french bread, pitta or wraps
100g of tinned (no added salt) or frozen sweetcorn
steps: Preheat oven to 180ºC/160ºC Fan/350ºF/Gas 4. Cover a baking tray with greaseproof paper, and place either the French bread, pitta or wraps on top.

Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat, then add the corn, red peppers, chicken and garlic. Fry for a further 2 minutes, until thoroughly cooked through. Remove from the heat and stir in the tomato puree.
Share out the chicken mixture evenly between bases then top with a blob of cream cheese and grated cheddar cheese.
Bake in the oven for 3-5 minutes or until the cheese melts and the base goes slightly crisp. Remove from the oven and sprinkle each pizza with the chopped basil.
hints: Serve with polenta fries, rice or pasta.

title: Butternut squash and broccoli purée
description: Try this weaning recipe which can be part of your baby's first foods. Step-by-step recipe for Butternut squash & broccoli purée!
ingredients: 100ml breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian)
Other vegetables you could add with butternut squash include carrots, peas or spinach
steps: Peel the butternut squash, scoop out the middle and chop into small pieces.
Chop the broccoli into small pieces.
Boil the butternut squash for approximately 8-10 minutes.
Add the broccoli to cook for a further 5 minutes.
Drain water and allow vegetables to cool.
Add 100ml breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian).
Use a blender to whizz up to a purée consistency.
Add more breast milk, standard infant formula or the specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed if a thinner consistency required.
Add into ice cube trays and freeze or use straight away.

title: Strawberry Ice Lolly
description: Enjoy a delicious Strawberry Ice Lolly, made with strawberry jam. This refreshing treat is perfect for summer, easy to make, and packed with flavor
steps: Mix the Renastep with the strawberry jam until completely combined.
Pour into lolly moulds and allow to freeze for 24 hours.

title: Stew
description: This slow cook diced lamb, parsnip and carrot stew recipe, has limited ingredients, but plenty of taste. Ideal for days where you can take your time cooking.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and allow the meat to brown. Once the meat has started to go brown, add in the parsnips and carrots, cook for 5 minutes.
Pour over 1000ml low salt beef stock and allow to come to the boil.
Once boiling, reduce to a simmer and allow to cook for 2 hours or until the meat is tender and falling apart.
Add in the Worcestershire sauce, stir well and serve.
hints: Serve with bread of your choice to soak up the sauce!
Renastep note
Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Simit Bread
description: Try this kidney-friendly Simit bread recipe – a soft, sesame-crusted Turkish classic made with low-sodium ingredients and perfect for everyday enjoyment
ingredients: 135g Strong white bread flour (a little extra flour will be needed for dusting)
½ tbsp Pomegranate molasses or molasses syrup
steps: Warm the Renastep gently in a pan to no more than 30˚C. Meanwhile, mix the flour and sugar in a bowl.
Add the dried yeast and Renastep and mix well until a soft dough is formed.
Place the dough onto a clean work surface dusted with flour. Knead the dough for for 5 minutes until the dough feels stretchy.
Place the dough in a clean bowl, cover and leave to prove for an hour, until doubled in size.
Heat oven to 200˚C/180˚C fan/gas mark 6.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan for 2-3 minutes until golden and set aside.
Mix the pomegranate molasses or molasses syrup with 50ml water in a shallow bowl.
When the dough has risen, roll out onto a clean, dusted work surface into a sausage shape about 45cm long and cut in half.
Place the two pieces lengthways together continuously twist them over each other for the full length of dough. Cut the twist into 2 equal pieces. Brush both sides with the molasses water.

Pour the toasted sesame seeds onto a piece of parchment paper and roll each twist of dough through the seeds until well covered. On a baking tray, join the ends of each twist to form two circles, cover and leave to prove for another 10 minutes.
When the bread has risen, uncover and bake for 15-18 mins until golden. Allow to cool before serving.

title: Rice Milk Pudding
description: Cook this rice milk pudding made with pudding rice, milk, cream, and cinnamon. A comforting low-sodium dessert suitable for kidney disease diets.
steps: Heat a pan on a medium heat and add the rice, milk, cream, water and sugar. Mix well until combined.
Allow to gently simmer for 1 hour, stirring regulatory to ensure it does not stick or burn.
Once the rice is cooked, stir in the vanilla essence and cinnamon.
Allow to cook for a further 10 minutes.
Serve and enjoy!

title: Orzo Soup
description: Taking just 15 minutes to make, this tasty orzo soup recipe has a handful ingredients. Making it a great lunch option or for a quick tea.
steps: Place the orzo into a pan, add 400ml of low salt vegetable stock and bring to the boil. Cook until the orzo is soft.
Turn off the heat and place the peas into the orzo. Allow to cook until warmed through.
Stir in the lemon juice and cheddar until the cheese melts.
Serve and enjoy.
hints: Renastep note
Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Alu sabudana tikki
description: This kidney-friendly Alu Sabudana Tikki recipe is made with sago, potatoes, and mild spices making a low-sodium snack. It takes just 20 minutes to cook.
steps: Wash sago (2-3 times) and soak for 6-7 hours or overnight. Once soaked, drain and rinse again.
Boil potatoes for 10 minutes, drain and grate them. Mix sago with grated potatoes and set aside.
To the mixture add ginger, garlic, turmeric and chilli powder (optional).
Add 1 tsp arrowroot/cornflour and mix all of it well to form a soft dough.
Grease hand with oil and prepare ball-sized tikki (patty).
Shallow fry in hot oil. Roast on low flame until it turns golden brown.
Flip over and cook on both sides.

title: Shai paneer
description: Learn how to make this creamy shahi paneer in a rich, flavourful, spiced cashew-tomato dish - perfect with naan or rice, made with Renastep.
steps: Heat the oil in a pan and add in the almonds, cashews and cardamom pods, fry until golden and remove from pan.
Add in the ginger, garlic, green chilli and onions and cook until soft.
Add everything into a blender and blend to a smooth paste, some water may be added to achieve a smoother consistency.
In the same pan heat oil and add in the cumin seeds, cinnamon stick and cloves and allow to sizzle for 30 seconds.
Then add in the garam masala, turmeric and nut paste and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add in the water and bubble for around 10 minutes.
Add in the Renastep and allow to warm through.
Once warmed add in paneer, cook for 1 minute and turn off the heat.
Serve with rice and enjoy.

title: Pina Colada Style Ice Lolly
description: Refreshing Piña Colada Style Ice Lolly: A tropical treat blending coconut and pineapple flavors for a delicious, cool, and creamy summer dessert.
steps: Finely dice or blend the pineapple.
Pour the coconut milk and Renastep into a jug.
Add the pineapple to the jug, mix the pineapple and pour into the lolly mould.
Allow to freeze for 24 hours.
hints: Renastep note

title: Muhalabieh
steps: Pour the Renastep and water into a pan and warm on a low to medium heat.
Add the sugar, cornflour and rose water and whisk continuously for 3-4 minutes until the mixture starts to thicken.
Remove from the heat (it will continue to thicken when chilled).
Line a bowl with cling film and pour the mixture in.
Let the mixture cool at room temperature for 30 minutes, then transfer to the fridge and chill for 2-3 hours or overnight if possible.
When chilled, loosen the cling film, and flip the pudding over on to plate.
Serve garnished with pistachios (if permitted) and rose petals.
hints: Water can be replaced with Renastep. Use a warm knife to smooth the top of the pudding before serving.

title: Double-Boiled Wedges and Aioli
ingredients: 350g red skin potatoes, peeled and sliced into wedges
steps: Boil the potatoes in a large amount of water for 10 minutes, this helps the potato lose some of its potassium.
Pour away the water.
Now boil the potatoes in fresh water for a further 10 minutes and again pour away the water once the potatoes are cooked. This lowers the potassium content even further.
Always ensure to pour away the water. The water should not be used for sauces or cooking other ingredients.
Once drained, place the wedges onto a baking tray, drizzle with vegetable oil, mixed herbs and black pepper.
Bake for 20 – 25 minutes or until golden brown.
While baking mix together the mayonnaise and garlic until well combined, place into a small bowl and set aside.
Once cooked serve the wedges immediately with the aioli and enjoy!
hints: Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Pierogi (Polish Dumplings)
description: Discover how to make our take on Pierogi the moreish Polish dumplings, for those on a renal diet. This recipe takes 20 minutes to cook and makes 4 portions.
steps: To make the dough
Place the flour into a bowl and make a ‘well’ in the middle. Add the egg, melted butter and hot water.
To make the dough
Mix together until a dough forms.
To make the dough
Turn onto a board and knead dough until smooth. Roll into a ball, cover and set aside for 20 minutes.
To make the filling
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and add the minced garlic and chopped onion. Fry until the onions become translucent.
To make the filling
Add in the minced beef and fry until browned.
To make the filling
Add in the grated carrot, black pepper and oregano and cook for a further 3 minutes.
Assembly
Roll out dough into a 10” (25cm) to 11” (28cm) circle. Cut 12 circles in the dough with a 3” (8cm) round cookie cutter.
Assembly
Place a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle of each dough circle. Fold over, stretch and press sides together to form a crescent-shaped dumpling
Assembly
In a large saucepan of boiling water, carefully place two or three dumplings in the water. The pierogi will float to the top when done. Remove with a slotted spoon and place onto kitchen paper.
Assembly
Once boiled, lightly fry the pierogi in the remaining 1 tbsp of olive oil over a medium heat. Fry for 3 minutes on each side until crispy and golden brown.
Creamy Cheese Sauce
In a pan, on a low heat add the Renastep, cream cheese, mixed herbs and garlic powder and stir until combined.
Creamy Cheese Sauce
Simmer for 3 minutes until thickened (do not boil).
Creamy Cheese Sauce
Divide the cheese sauce over the 4 portions of Pierogi.
hints: Renastep note

title: Gingery Cookies
description: Try baking our deliciously spiced Gingery Cookies recipe, perfect for anyone who loves a warm, flavorful treat. This easy recipe makes 18 cookies.
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C/160°C Fan/350° F/Gas 4.
In a large bowl, cream together the butter and sugar.
Add the golden syrup and dry ingredients and beat to combine.
Once everything is combined, using your hands (make sure they are clean!) roll the mixture out into little balls, keeping each even in size.
Place 3cm apart on a greased baking tray and lightly press down using a fork.
Bake in the oven for 15 minutes or until golden brown.

title: Hünkar Beğendi
description: Cook this kidney-friendly Hünkar Beğendi recipe with tender turkey in tomato sauce served over creamy roasted aubergine purée to make a delicious meal.
steps: Place the aubergines under a hot grill and allow to char on all sides, remove from the grill and allow to cool.
Once cooled peel the aubergines charred skin and set aside.
Heat oil and flour in a pan and stir to form a paste.
Add the roasted aubergines to the pan, once heated mash the aubergines to form a smooth paste.
Reduce the heat and gradually add in the Renastep, black pepper and nutmeg to the mixture and stir well until combined.
Allow to cook for a further 2 minutes and then set aside.
In a separate pan, heat oil in a pan and add in the turkey chunks. Allow to cook until browned.
Add the onions and peppers to the meat and cook until softened.
Add in the grated tomato mixture and the additional water, allow to cook until the sauce has reduced and the meat is fully cooked.
Serve on top of the roasted aubergine puree and serve.
hints: Renastep note
Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Roasted red pepper soup
description: Learn how to make this smoky roasted red pepper soup blended smooth with herbs and cream - rich, vibrant, and comforting in every warm spoonful.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Place the red pepper, onions and sweet potatoes into a baking tray with the garlic.
Drizzle over the olive oil, then add the paprika, chilli flakes and black pepper, mix thoroughly until the vegetables are evenly coated .
Roast in the oven for 35 minutes or until soft.
Once cooked add to pan with the low salt stock and Renastep and cook on a medium heat until warmed through.
When warm, blend until smooth, serve and enjoy!

title: Burrito Bowl
description: This Burrito Bowl recipe with tofu, pepper, harissa, peas and onions has been created for those with kidney disease. Ideal for a weekend meal.
ingredients: 5g fresh coriander, finely chopped (reserve some for garnish)
steps: Heat water in a pan. When it’s boiling, add rice and cook for 10 minutes and set aside
Add the tofu, cornflour, and ground coriander to a bowl. Stir until the tofu is well coated with cornflour.
Heat a small amount of oil in a frying pan and add the coated tofu. Cook until golden brown all over and set aside.
Heat oil in a frying pan and add garlic, harissa, black beans, and ½ the lime juice. Allow to fry until hot and then set aside.
For the pico de gallo add red pepper, onion and coriander to a small bowl. Stir well and set aside.
In a blender, add the peas, lime juice, and olive oil and blend until combined but still retaining some texture
Serve rice into a bowl and top with the tofu, black beans, pico de gallo, pea guacamole and coconut yoghurt. Sprinkle with coriander and serve!
hints: Renastep note
Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Vegetable Risotto
description: Try our flavorful vegetable risotto recipe, specially designed for a renal diet. Enjoy a delicious and nourishing meal that supports your medical dietary needs. Cook it today!
steps: If using peas: Put the peas into a pan of water and boil for 5 minutes, then drain. If using broccoli: Remove the chunky stem and discard. Chop the florets evenly and boil in a pan of water for 5 minutes and drain. If using courgette: Cut the ends off the courgette and throw them away. Slice the courgette, boil in a pan of water for 5 minutes and drain.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan and add the onion and garlic, cook over a medium heat for 5 minutes, or until the onion is soft.
Take the pan off the heat and add the rice, stirring until the rice is coated with the oil.
In a jug, add 850ml boiling water to the stock cube and stir until dissolved.

Using a ladle, add one scoop of the stock to the rice mixture, and put back on the heat. Gently stir the rice until nearly all the liquid has been absorbed. Each time the stock is absorbed, add another ladleful.
About 15 minutes after you added the first stock, stir in the precooked vegetables. Keep adding ladles of stock and stirring them in, until the rice is creamy and just tender.
Take the pan off the heat and cover it with a lid. Leave it for 3 minutes, then stir in the parsley, parmesan and 2 pinches of pepper.

title: Cheese Muffins
description: These delightful savoury muffins are a great way to incorporate Renastep into your lunch. Made with just a few ingredients they take just 10 minutes to prepare.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C/356°F/Gas mark 4
Mix the olive oil and Renastep in a jug and set aside.
Whisk the egg well until pale and fluffy.
Place the flour in a bowl and mix in the olive oil and Renastep mixture, once fully combined gently fold in the egg mixture.
Fold in the grated cheddar and set aside.
Divide equally between 6 muffin cases and bake for 25 minutes or until golden brown and fully cooked.
Leave to cool, serve and enjoy!
hints: Renastep note
Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Christmas tree pizza base and topping
description: Get into the festive spirit with this renal diet friendly Christmas Tree Pizza made with Renastep. Try cooking this recipe to see how colourful yours can be!
steps: For the base
Preheat the oven to 200°C/180°C Fan/Gas Mark 6.
For the base
Place the Renastep and yeast into a mixing bowl and stir until combined.
For the base
Add the flour, sugar and oil to the Renastep and yeast mixture and mix together by hand until a dough forms. Knead for 2 minutes
For the base
Leave the dough to rise for 60 minutes in a warm place.
For the base

Lightly dust a clean work surface with flour and roll the dough ball into a rectangle 22cm long and 13cm wide. Using a knife, cut a diagonal line from the centre of the top of the rectangle to the bottom left and right corners to create a triangle shape.
For the base
Place the triangle onto a baking tray lined with grease proof paper. Use the remaining dough to make a small tree trunk at the bottom of the triangle – stick this to the tree with a drop of oil.
For the topping
To make the pesto, blend the basil, oil and garlic together in a bowl, using a hand blender.
For the topping
Take your pizza base and cover the tree with pesto using the back of a spoon to spread. Leave a border around the edge.
For the topping
Place the sliced pepper and red onion across the tree in rows to resemble tinsel.
For the topping
Sprinkle Violife mozzarella style over the pizza
For the topping
To make a star, slice a large carrot lengthways to make a thin slice, cut out a star shape and place at the top of the tree.
For the topping
Cook the base and topping in the oven at 200°C/180°C Fan/Gas Mark 6 for approximately 15 minutes. Serve warm.
hints: Renastep note
Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision.

title: Polenta Chips
description: This easy to make fried snack has been created so that renal patients can enjoy a low potassium chip alternative. Cook along with the Chef Neil.
ingredients: 200ml reduced salt chicken or vegetable stock, or water
steps: Bring the stock to a boil in a saucepan and add the polenta in a steady stream. Cook, stirring continuously, for 5 minutes (take care as polenta bubbles furiously).
Take off the heat and stir in the parmesan (if using).

Spoon the mixture onto the tray and flatten into a large rectangular shape, about 5-10 mm thick (depending on how thick you want your chips!) using the back of the wooden spoon. Leave to cool for 10-15 minutes.

Add the chips to a baking tray and brush with oil. Bake in the oven on a medium heat (180ºC) for 15 minutes until golden brown. Alternatively, shallow fry the chips in oil, frying lightly and evenly on all 4 sides. Serve hot and enjoy! This recipe is taken from the Kidney Friendly Cookbook produced by Dietitians and Dietetic Support Workers at a Paediatric Renal Unit in the UK. Please check with your Dietitian or Doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Bialys
description: Learn how to make this soft, chewy kidney-friendly bialys with low sodium and balanced protein - a perfect savory snack filled with flavour.
steps: Mix together the flour, garlic powder and yeast in a bowl.
Create a well and pour in the warm water and stir to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes or until smooth then place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and allow to prove for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, heat oil in a pan and add the onions, garlic, and black pepper and soften for 5 minutes.
Stir in the poppy seeds and remove the pan from the heat and set aside.
Once proved divide the dough into 8 equal portions and shape into balls.
Press down the centre of each ball to create a dent. Pick up and spin slowly through your hands so the dough in the centre becomes thinner, ensuring not to rip the centre.
Repeat this process for all 8 balls.
Place all the bialys onto a baking tray and evenly distribute the filling into the centre of each one.
Bake for 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Serve and enjoy!
